A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PDR-Bench and PQR evaluation study. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support comparison of all main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-J, including the shifted appendix pages.

before.justification: v2 reports original agent evaluations, memory-system comparisons, and alignment with human ratings in Section 5, with further results and running costs in Appendices F-G.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including the main agent evaluations, memory-system comparisons, human-rating study, and appendix results.

M1.justification: The PQR procedure retains identical dynamic weighting, criterion generation, scoring, factual verification, and aggregation steps in Section 4. Appendix J's evaluation prompts are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain 50 tasks across 10 domains, 25 user profiles, and 250 task-user pairs. The evaluated Task Only, Task w/Context, and Task w/Persona scenarios remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The evaluated agent, search-LLM, memory-system, and judge-model sets are unchanged across corresponding comparisons. O-Mem already appears in v2's Table 3; v3 adds its citation without adding or replacing a comparator.

E3.justification: Both retain the 150-query main evaluation, 50-query memory experiment, and 15-query human-alignment study. Judge models, metrics, query selection, agent configurations, and execution budgets in Section 5 and Appendix B are unchanged.

E4.justification: The information-availability analysis, memory-system experiment, human-alignment validation, and marathon-planning case study are retained without revision in Sections 5.3-5.5 and Appendices G-H.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Both versions report the same point-estimate results without adding repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results, costs, and qualitative findings in Tables 1-4 and 8-9 and Figures 3-4 are identical. For example, O-Mem's Table 3 P-Score remains 4.26, and GPT-5's Table 4 PCA and MARD remain 0.43 and 1.40.

T1.justification: The benchmark definitions, PQR scoring equations, and Appendix C definitions of PCA and MARD are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about introducing personalized deep research evaluation, PDR-Bench, and the PQR framework. Their scientific scope and novelty claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Sections 5.2-5.5 retain the same interpretations of personalization, reliability, context use, and memory limitations. Appendix A's qualifications about Chinese linguistic and cultural coverage and evaluation on a subset are identical.

D1.justification: Section 7 expands the earlier anonymization statement by specifying de-identified, abstracted profile derivatives without PII and consent covering public release. This adds data-handling disclosure without establishing changed experimental processing. Configurations, annotation instructions, prompts, and Section 8's release instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Wang et al. (2025b), O-Mem: Omni Memory System for Personalized, Long Horizon, Self-Evolving Agents, replacing Section 5.4's description of O-Mem as a private agent memory system with a citation. The broader related-work discussion and research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 locally rewrites and expands the ethics statement, adds acknowledgments and funding information, replaces the work-in-progress header with ICLR 2026 publication wording, and fills bibliographic access-date placeholders. The scientific narrative and section organization remain otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: The longer ethics statement and new acknowledgments reflow the bibliography, and page headers change. Figures 1-4 and Tables 1-9 retain their visual designs and content; all appendix body layouts match after accounting for shifted pagination.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency through more specific reporting of institutional ethical approval, participant rights, and privacy safeguards in Section 7, and improves attribution by identifying O-Mem. These are limited documentation gains; the scientific evidence is unchanged. Section 8's retained future-release wording still leaves actual release status unclear.
